To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
subjective estimation of mood/activation is correlated with EEG spectral power parameters.
the EEG spectral power parameters co-varied with subjective mood estimation.

(a) subjective estimation of mood is correlated with spectral power characteristics of EEG; (b) this co-variance is different for the two mood dimensions, and (c) the correlation is different for different EEG frequency bands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether subjective mood estimation is related to EEG parameters.
the relation between subjective estimation of mood and EEG characteristics.
the relation between subjective and objective measures of mood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mood estimation is related to EEG characteristics in a complex manner and the results of this study should be interpreted as a first step in a long-term investigation.
mood estimation is not a unitary phenomenon, but is rather a complex multidimensional process, and the EEG correlates reflect the multidimensional structure of the phenomenon.
EEG spectral parameters are not a reliable indicator of the subjectively estimated mood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
subjective mood estimation is not only related to the brain activity in the frontal lobe but also in other brain structures.
the EEG correlates of mood are not limited to the alpha band and are not necessarily related to the arousal component of the activation-deactivation dimension of the mood.
the EEG characteristics of the brain are related to the subjective experience of mood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subjective assessment of mood is not only an important aspect of the clinical practice of psychiatry, but it also has an objective counterpart in EEG spectral power characteristics.
the brain correlates of the subjective mood estimation are frequency-specific, and are localized in the frontal and parietal areas.
subjective mood estimation is not a random phenomenon, but rather a measurable and reproducible brain state, and thus it can be used as a valid and useful measure of brain function.
